newsitem.title: THAILAND: HSBC to expand Thai retail banking.
newsitem.headline: HSBC to expand Thai retail banking.

text.p: Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp Ltd said on Wednesday it would sharply expand its retail banking service in Thailand to offset its current business dominated by corporate and trade financing.
HongkongBank country manager Richard Cromwell said his bank is seeking to raise the number of its Thai credit cards to 50,000 by end-1997 from slightly over 20,000 now.
"The number would help achieve a critical mass that will allow us to do other cross selling," he told reporters.

Cromwell said HongkongBank, the first foreign bank to open a branch in Thailand in 1865 and unit of HSBC Holdings Plc, would also be active in providing personal housing loans despite a prolonged property sector slowdown.

He said his bank's planned expansion into the retail sector got a major boost last month when it and Standard Chartered Bank were the first foreign banks allowed to join a 3,300 automatic telling machines pool operated by Thai banks.
Cromwell said he hoped personal banking will generate 50 percent of HongkongBank's overall business in Thailand in five years from less than 10 percent now.
He said the focus on retail banking, including telephone banking service being introduced in March, would require the bank to increase its Thai staff to over 1,000 in five years from 460 now.
HongkongBank is seeking to expand its one-branch operation in Thailand by upgrading two provincial offshore banking offices in northern Chiangmai and eastern Chonburi provinces into full branches.
